Make Your Visit Easier Opening Hours : Monday through Friday: 9 a.m. – 4 p.m. Saturday and Sunday: 10 a.m. – 5 p.m. Customer service Contact form Phone: 514-496-4724 or 1-877-496-4724 Customer service hours: Monday to Friday: 2 pm to 4 pm Saturday and Sunday: 10 am to 3 pm For all school group booking requests BOOK YOUR SCHOOL VISIT Frequently Asked Questions Can't find an answer to your question on this page? Visit our FAQ ! Location The Montréal Science Centre is located in the Old Port of Montréal, at the foot of St. Laurent Blvd., corner of de la Commune Street (Place-d'Armes metro station). SCIENCE CENTRE MAP See the map Parking Rates (taxes included)* Less than 2 hours: $20 $25 $30 $35 $40 Less than 24 hours: Up to $90 Lost parking ticket $70 Bus (valid for 12 hours, subject to availability) $50 Monthly + taxes (Individual) - November 1 through April 30 $240 Ticket available for one entry/exit. *Payable at the exit. In case of any discrepancy between the information provided on this website and those provided at the parking gate, the information from the parking gate prevails. Payments methods Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Interac, Google Pay, Apple Pay. Payment at the exit gate or at the payment terminal before leaving. Contact us Monday to Friday from 8am to 4pm. 514 496-1851 stationnement@vieuxportdemontreal.com To book an appointment, click here . Public Transit By metro Place d'Armes metro station By bus Line 75 de la Commune (McGill / Wellington stop) Map - Line 75 - Schedule - Line 75 Line 55 Saint-Laurent (Saint-Laurent / Saint-Jacques stop) Map - Line 55 - Schedule - Line 55 Line 50 Vieux-Montréal/Vieux-Port Map - Line 50 - Schedule - Line 50 For other options, visit the Montréal public transit website: www.stm.info Commuter train Lucien-L’Allier train station is connected to Lucien-L’Allier metro station. The Central Station train station is connected to Bonaventure metro station www.amt.qc.ca River shuttle From Longueuil, Boucherville, Pointe-aux-Trembles, Varennes, Ile Sainte-Hélène : visit Navark . Monthly parking By email: complete the downloadable contract here and send it to us at the email address below. Online: click here to be directed to our online sales site Rates : $240 per month from November to April, $310 per month from May to October. Plus taxes. FAQ King Edward Quay (Montréal Science Centre) There are 4 charging points available for electric vehicles at a rate of $2 per hour. To access the charging points, you must pay the current price of a parking space, which is not included in the cost of recharging.Four electric vehicle charging stations (free). Clock Tower Quay Located at a few minutes away from the Science Centre. Disabled Parking Permit 28 parking spaces for permit holders spread across our two parkings. To ensure accessibility to our parking lots, holders of a permit for people with mobility impairment can exit without having to pay parking fees by contacting our team using the assistance button at the exit. Bus Parking (School and Tour Groups) Free parking for up to 14 school buses at the Clock Tower Quay parking lot. Free access for groups visiting the Montréal Science Centre. Passengers disembark on the central aisle, west side (building side) after the entrance marked IMAX®Telus. Ask your group sales agent for information: groupsales@montrealsciencecentre.com or 514-496-2281. Please note: RVs and vehicles with trailers are not allowed in our parking lots. Accessibility Science Centre receives the Kéroul “Accessible site for people with physical limitations” certification, confirming its commitment to accessibility. Free wheelchairs Wheelchairs are available to ticket holders. Limited quantity. Hearing Impaired and Deaf Visitors An assistive listening system is available at the IMAX®TELUS theatre, as well as a frequency-modulated (FM) signal for visitors with their own device. The vast majority of videos available in the Science Centre's exhibitions are subtitled in both official languages. Guide accompagnying people with special needs This guide was designed to help you plan your visit at the Centre and for easy referral while on site. The guide offers an overview of the Centre’s various environments, the various quiet spots and changing places as well as the content of all our exhibitions. This should help you better choose the activities most suited to you. The guide includes all the information you’ll need to make the very best of your visit! EXHIBITIONS: DOWNLOAD THE GUIDE FEATURED EXHIBITION: DOWNLOAD THE GUIDE On-site catering Café Van Houtte Coffee – Tea – Ready-to-eat Specialty Coffee Sandwiches and Hot Meals Pastries Desserts and Snacks Breakfast Salads and Soups Boutique Lunch room Tables are available to visitors to eat a meal. Please note that there are no microwaves. Sanitary measures are applied to maintain safety. Groups have priority to use our lunch rooms during weekdays. Rebates The Montréal Science Centre is proud to extend these exclusive offers from our partners. See rebatES Donation Form To request a donation in tickets, please complete the following form: REQUEST FOR DONATION IN TICKETS Rules and regulations Eating and drinking is prohibited in the Montréal Science Centre exhibition halls. All visitors must pay Montréal Science Centre entry fees. It is prohibited to film, take photos, and make recordings during an IMAX®TELUS theatre film screening without the authorization of the Corporation. It is forbidden to surpass the maximum capacity of Montréal Science Centre halls and to obstruct its stairways, passageways, and emergency routes. All groups visiting the Montréal Science Centre must be accompanied by group leaders, follow the directives of Corporation employees, respect the time of their visit, and ensure the spaces they use are kept calm and in good order. Children under 13 years of age visiting the Montréal Science Centre must be accompanied by an adult. Being naked, bare-footed, or wearing indecent or offensive clothing is forbidden at the Montréal Science Centre. Shoes, pants or shorts, and shirts are mandatory everywhere at the Centre including, but not limited to, inside its buildings. Working animals (guide dogs and assistance dogs), whether on duty or in training, are allowed inside the Science Center building. Unfortunately, pets are not accepted. En explorant ce milieu unique, vous apprendrez à identifier les différentes espèces. 6 octobre 2026 au 2 mai 2027 Planétarium Rencontres dans la Voie lactée Explorez notre galaxie, découvrez son histoire et son avenir, ainsi que les transformations dynamiques qui s’y produisent sans cesse. Remontant à des milliards d’années dans le passé et se projetant des millions d’années dans l’avenir, Rencontres dans la Voie lactée est un voyage spatio-temporel à la découverte des mouvements cosmiques qui structurent notre voisinage galactique. 3 octobre 2026 au 17 avril 2027 Biosphère Samedi famille Le premier et troisième samedi du mois, de décembre à avril, la Biosphère vous propose de découvrir en famille l’une ou l’autre de ses expositions sous un angle nouveau en compagnie d’artistes, de scientifiques et de citoyens et citoyennes qui ont à cœur l’environnement.
